items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' after the greeting.
No agenda statement (what will happen on the call / how long it takes) and no explicit 'sound good?' before jumping into profile-building.
Never asked about stairs or floors at either the origin or destination.
Never asked about narrow hallways, tight turns, or other special-access considerations.
Never asked whether the customer wanted or needed packing services.
Never asked about access concerns — elevator, parking, HOA restrictions.
Never asked a moving-stressors question like 'Is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?'
Skipped the 'pricing is super simple' opener before launching into the rate breakdown.
Never mentioned packing service pricing.
Never mentioned No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000 per move).
Never mentioned Meet Your Mover (photo + info email before the move).
Never mentioned the On-Time Guarantee.
Never delivered the full 'no hidden fees' pitch (no CC fees, no transportation/fuel surcharge, no assembly fees).
Didn't state that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens.
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check after explaining the clock/pricing structure.
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped — no consolidation tips (drawers, garden tools, wall photos) and no 'take a carload' tip, despite the customer being visibly unsure of her own box count.
Didn't ask 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never stated branch hours or how to reach the office.
Didn't explain the 'reply with any corrections' step for the confirmation email.
Never mentioned the BOLDED key-details list at the top of the confirmation email.
Used the customer's name only twice (Kristen), short of the 3+ threshold.
Restated the total inconsistently ($2,678 vs. customer hearing $2,378), forcing the customer to ask for the numbers twice.
Insurance was only referenced in passing ('insurance that we placed on your move') — no No Worries / 60¢-per-lb baseline explanation.
top_strength: Erik ran a thorough room-by-room inventory (bedrooms, living/dining, kitchen, garage, and patio) and proactively right-sized the crew from the standard 4 movers/2 trucks to 3 movers/1 truck, cross-checking Fort Worth vs. Dallas rates to land the customer a lower total — strong budget-conscious framing that clearly resonated with a price-sensitive, returning-customer referral.
coaching_note: Erik skipped the Save Your Ass prep speech entirely — with a customer already bouncing between 15 and 30+ boxes on her garage estimate alone, a quick consolidation/carload tip is the single highest-leverage thing missing here, since it directly ties to shortening the move and tightening the estimate (Cameron's estimate-accuracy priority).
phone_presence_notes: Consistent, natural warmth throughout ('yes ma'am,' 'no worries,' 'I love that'), including patient re-explanations when the customer got confused on the total, and the customer's own account of loving Einstein enough to call back confirms the rapport landed.
